statement: For the unit-intensity sine determinantal point process with kernel k(x)=sin(pi*x)/(pi*x), S_R its sinc-Gram matrix on [0,R], and mu_R=R^(-1) E sum_j delta_(lambda_j(S_R)), every fixed nonnegative integer moment has a finite limit as R tends to infinity. These limits have the absolutely convergent anchored partition-integral formula in the cited proof. The deterministic expected per-length laws mu_R consequently converge weakly to a unique probability law, which has no atom at zero, is moment determinate, and has a positive exponential moment.
hypotheses: Stationary sine DPP on the full real line; intensity one; expected per-length law, not random point-count normalization. Moment order is fixed before R tends to infinity. No arithmetic moment-matching hypothesis is established.
proof_dependencies: Closed trace-cycle quotient is a connected Eulerian multigraph; after removal of loops it has no bridges

For a connected bridgeless multigraph, uniform spanning-tree edge inclusion probabilities theta_e lie strictly between zero and one; generalized Holder and rooted-tree integration imply anchored absolute integrability of the product of sinc edge kernels
Stationarity and exact interval-overlap factor permit dominated convergence for each finite set partition
